A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDB framework and two debiasing recipes. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite retitling and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, synthetic-image analyses, Waterbirds ablations and unbiased CIFAR-10 experiments.

after.justification: v4 retains original experimental results and adds ImageNet-A and UrbanCars evaluations, synthetic-image bias proportions and bias-identification measurements.

M1.justification: The conditional diffusion generator, synthetic-only Bias Amplifier training, filtered pseudo-labeling with G-DRO, and frozen-amplifier loss reweighting remain unchanged. Appendix A.3 explicitly applies Recipe I unchanged to UrbanCars; its additional subgroup description does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: v4 removes Corrupted CIFAR-10 and adds ImageNet-9 training with ImageNet-A evaluation, plus UrbanCars with simultaneous background and co-occurring-object biases. Waterbirds, BAR, BFFHQ and the ordinary CIFAR-10 sanity checks remain.

E2.justification: Compared with v1 Table 2, v4 Table 1 adds CDvG+LfF on Waterbirds and BFFHQ, LWBC on BAR, and ETF-Debias and Park et al. on BFFHQ. The new UrbanCars comparison also introduces LLE and EIIL. These are substantive additions to evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: New protocols include ImageNet-9-to-ImageNet-A evaluation and UrbanCars training with four inferred groups followed by evaluation across eight groups using ID accuracy and subgroup gaps. v4 also adds overall BFFHQ accuracy. Its main text reports three image annotators instead of two, although Appendix A.7 still states two.

E4.justification: v4 removes both recipes' controlled bias-correlation sweeps from v1 Tables 3 and 5, eliminating direct failure-boundary tests. It also removes BFFHQ and BAR caption-frequency analyses, while adding Bias Amplifier identification accuracy on Waterbirds and BFFHQ. Sample-count, guidance-strength and unbiased-data analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three independent runs and mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting for main classification results. Retained sample-count and guidance-strength ablations still report point estimates. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or seed-reporting practice appear.

E6.justification: The existing DDB scores on Waterbirds, BAR and BFFHQ conflicting accuracy remain unchanged. v4 adds overall BFFHQ accuracy, ImageNet-A results of 39.80% for DDB-I and 37.53% for DDB-II, UrbanCars results, and bias-identification measurements. Corrupted CIFAR-10 and correlation-sweep results are removed.

T1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same distributional assumptions, diffusion and guidance equations, pseudo-label filtering rule and relative-loss weighting. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs, and v4 introduces no substantive theoretical revision.

C1.justification: The central synthetic-bias-amplification and reusable debiasing-plugin claims remain. v4 explicitly extends its contribution claims to single and multiple biases and strengthens the conclusion from suitability for real-world debiasing to an effective general-purpose standard training procedure.

C2.justification: v1 explains how increasing bias-conflicting generations degrades both recipes at training correlation 0.700; v4 removes this substantive applicability boundary. It adds interpretations of UrbanCars subgroup balance and the recipes' differing residual biases. Computational-cost and small-dataset limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 newly documents split sizes for retained datasets and provides diffusion-training budgets, amplifier settings and backbone choices for ImageNet-9 and UrbanCars. Most existing implementation details are retained in Appendices A.2–A.4, while Corrupted CIFAR-10 settings disappear. Full recipe hyperparameters for the added benchmarks remain unspecified.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands comparisons with generative and augmentation-based debiasing, including Jung et al., DFA, BiasAdv and SelecMix. v4 explicitly claims priority for using generative models to obtain an amplified biased distribution, replacing much of the earlier general diffusion-bias discussion with closer methodological positioning.

P1.justification: Beyond the new title, v4 rewrites the abstract and substantial introductory passages, reorganizes related work into end-to-end and two-step discussions, moves detailed dataset and implementation descriptions into numbered appendices, and reorders supplementary material.

P2.justification: v4 removes the introductory snapshot, redraws the framework horizontally, and merges the two recipe diagrams into Figure 2. It expands the main comparison table, adds an UrbanCars table, revises image galleries and removes several analytical displays. Typography and page composition are substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: Broader evaluations, closer prior-work comparisons and direct bias-identification measurements strengthen v4. However, removing v1's correlation sweeps loses important failure-boundary evidence while the conclusion broadens to general-purpose training. The UrbanCars discussion emphasizes smaller gaps without addressing DDB-I's lower ID accuracy, 86.39% versus LLE's 96.70%. These substantive benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
